title: Morrey’s planar rank-one convexity versus quasiconvexity
decision_reason: Pedregal v5 (June 18, 2026) Theorems 1.1(2) and 1.2 claim exactly the planar implication. Earlier withdrawal does not adjudicate the new proof. No independent specialist adjudication of this revised argument was located; keep outside accepted count.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Finite-valued continuous W on real 2x2 matrices
problem_fingerprint.dimension: Two space and two target dimensions
problem_fingerprint.boundary_or_initial_conditions: Zero-trace Lipschitz test maps on bounded Lipschitz domains

statement_source_and_scope_match: Pedregal v5 introduction defines the precise notions, and Theorem 1.2 claims the full implication, not a symmetry-restricted subclass.
proposed_statement_text: Does every continuous rank-one-convex function W:R^(2x2)->R satisfy W(F) <= |D|^(-1) integral_D W(F+gradient phi) for every F, bounded Lipschitz D in R^2 and phi in W_0^(1,infinity)(D;R^2)?
applied_significance: Concerns whether stability of an elastic energy along rank-one directions suffices for stability under arbitrary fine-scale gradient perturbations in a planar variational model.

source_records.title: Morrey’s conjecture: rank-one convexity implies quasi-convexity for two-dimensional, two-component maps
